newsitem.title: FINLAND: Merita says dividend forecast unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Merita says dividend forecast unchanged.

text.p: Finland's largest banking group Merita Oy said on Wednesday its November forecast of dividends for 1996 on the preferential B shares and "a modest dividend also on A shares" is still in force.
"The old forecast is still in force," Merita spokesman Timo Nikinmaa told Reuters by telephone.

Merita last week announced that its pension fund would be able to return surplus contributions of 1.23 billion markka to the group, an extraordinary gain which will boost Merita's share capital, but this had not changed the dividend forecast, he said. @
"Good profits should not automatically be interpreted to be paid out as dividends," Nikinmaa said, adding that the group still needed to boost its capital structure.

Merita has some 4.1 billion of capital certificates from the government, interest payments of which totalled some 200 million markka in 1996, Nikinmaa said. The certificates will be repaid to the state when there are economic incentives to do so, he said.
Last year's interest rate on the capital certificates was 5.76 percent, a Merita spokeswoman said later.

Merita's 67.2 million preferential B shares have accumulated a right to 1.60 markka in dividends before the 763.3 million A shares can receive any, and if the A shares receive more than 0.80 markka, the B shares will get half the difference.
